subject: Clarifying pricing safeguards and CPI cap for committed hosted API usage
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@nimblehealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit — pricing safeguards questions

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. As we start building our procurement packet for a 12–24 month committed usage agreement, the procurement and finance teams at NimbleHealth have asked for clarity on a few contractual safeguards around pricing. They want to understand what protections Redwood will provide so we can justify the committed spend. Specifically: 

- Will Redwood provide a price lock for the duration of the committed term (i.e., guarantee per-token rates won't increase mid-term)?
- Do you offer an MFN (most-favored-nation) clause or similar that ensures we won't be charged more than other customers with comparable committed volume?
- How do you handle inflationary adjustments? Procurement prefers an explicit CPI-cap or a hard percent cap on annual increases.

A few additional operational clarifications: true-up cadence (monthly vs quarterly), how downgrades/overages are billed, and whether reserved capacity changes the protections above.

If you could send a short term-sheet or sample contract language we can share with our legal team that would be ideal. I attached the procurement checklist from our side for reference (see attachment).

Appreciate it — can we aim to have a follow-up by early next week?

Best,
Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform Procurement
NimbleHealth

Attachment: NimbleHealth_procurement_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit — pricing safeguards questions

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear list. I looped in Marcus (revenue ops) and Laura (finance/legal) so we can be precise. High-level responses below and I attached a short term sheet with proposed language: Commit_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf.

- Price lock: For fixed-term committed agreements (12–36 months) we can offer a contractual price lock on the agreed per-token tiers for the length of the commitment. The lock applies to the specific model family and region agreed in the SOW. It does not apply to new model variants that have materially different capabilities (we'll call that out in the contract).

- MFN: We can include a limited MFN that protects you against lower per-token prices offered to other customers with equivalent committed volume and similar contract length within the same region. We typically scope MFN to a 12-month lookback and to like-for-like commitment bands.

- Inflation / CPI cap: We're open to capping annual pricing adjustments. Our standard proposal is: fixed price for the first 12 months, then annual increases thereafter capped at the higher of CPI (US urban CPI-U) or 2.5%, with a hard cap of 4% in any year. If you prefer a single hard cap (e.g., no increases >2.5%), we can discuss — this tends to get tricker for long tails of multi-year hardware cost variation.

- True-ups & billing: We propose monthly metered billing with a quarterly reconciliation to simplify finance workflows. Overages are billed at the overage per-token rate defined in the term sheet; we also offer monthly reporting exports for easier validation.

- Reserved capacity: Dedicated/dedicated+ guarantees (Reserved GPU pools) can be priced separately; reserved capacity agreements typically come with firmer latency/availability SLAs and stable pricing, which makes price locks simpler to guarantee.

Next steps: Marcus will draft the MFN and CPI-cap clause language based on the options above and send an updated term sheet with two alternate CPI clauses (one CPI-floor hybrid, one fixed-percent cap) so you can show both to legal. Laura will review for finance/ASC 606 implications.

I'll follow up by EOD Thursday with the redlines.

Best,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Attachment: Commit_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (term sheet stub)

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@nimblehealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2026 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit — pricing safeguards questions

Thanks Ava — that helps and the term sheet looks like a good start. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal: 

- MFN scope: procurement is asking that MFN not be restricted to "like-for-like" language only; they'd like MFN to apply broadly to any published per-token pricing for committed customers at equal or greater volume tiers for the same region and model family within 12 months. Can you confirm if Redwood can accept that broader wording?

- CPI cap: NimbleHealth prefers a straight annual cap (no CPI indexing) — their target is max +2.5% per annum. If Redwood cannot accept a flat 2.5% cap, we need to understand worst-case scenarios; procurement will escalate if there's ambiguity.

- Price decreases: procurement also wants a downward adjustment mechanism — if Redwood reduces published pricing for comparable customers during our term, can we be credited the delta retroactively (i.e., true-up credits)?

I've attached our preferred redlines to the term sheet (NimbleHealth_redlines_20260630.pdf). Can Marcus and Laura please review and respond to the three core asks above? We need an internal decision by Friday to keep the budget cycle moving.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Sanjay

Attachment: NimbleHealth_redlines_20260630.pdf (annotated term sheet)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@nimblehealth.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit — pricing safeguards questions

Hi Sanjay — Marcus here (Revenue Ops). Thanks for the detailed redlines. Quick responses inline below; full proposed language is in the attached PDF (Commit_Term_Sheet_v2_REDLINE_RESPONSE.pdf).

- MFN: We can accept an MFN that applies to published per-token prices for committed customers in the same region and model family, provided the comparison is to customers with an equal or greater committed monthly token baseline and similar minimum term length (>=12 months). We cannot accept an MFN that is completely unrestricted (e.g., comparing to one-off promotional prices). We will add carve-outs for promotional/introductory offers and channel/partner discounts.

- CPI vs flat cap: We cannot guarantee a flat 2.5% cap across all possible market conditions for multi-year deals. Proposal: fixed price for year one, and thereafter annual increases limited to the lower of (i) 2.5% or (ii) the US CPI-U + 0.5 percentage points, with an absolute maximum of 3.5% in any year. This is designed to give you protection while allowing us limited headroom for underlying cost inflation (GPU/cloud, energy).

- Downward adjustment / credits: Yes — if Redwood publishes a lower committed per-token price to another qualifying customer during your term (per the MFN rules), NimbleHealth would be eligible for a retroactive credit for the difference on future invoices (not a cash refund). The credit mechanics and notice period are described in section 4(b) of the attached.

If that compromise is acceptable I can finalize the term-sheet language and send it back for your legal review. Also cc'ing Laura for confirmation on accounting treatment and any ASC 606 notes.

On timing — we can turn around a revised term sheet today if you confirm the MFN carve-outs above are acceptable.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachment: Commit_Term_Sheet_v2_REDLINE_RESPONSE.pdf (response + proposed language)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Final proposal and next steps — NimbleHealth commit (RDW-2026-NH-87)

Sanjay — Laura from Finance/Legal here. Marcus and I reviewed the redlines and (per our exchange) attached the finalized term sheet with the negotiated language. Key points summarized: 

- Price lock: confirmed for model family/region for the agreed term; year one fixed.
- MFN: applies to published committed pricing for equal-or-greater volume bands in-region and for the same model family; excludes limited-time promos, channel partner discounts, and pilot programs.
- Annual increase: capped at the lower of 2.5% or CPI-U + 0.5%, with an absolute maximum of 3.5% in any calendar year.
- Downward credits: retroactive credits for qualifying lower published prices; applied to future invoices.
- Billing/true-up: monthly metered billing, quarterly reconciliation.

I've also included a short note on accounting: the credit mechanics are consistent with our revenue accounting practices and should be manageable for your team's finance team (we included an example calculation in the PDF).

If this matches your expectations we can (a) upload the term sheet to DocuSign and (b) create a HubSpot deal with the SOW attached. I'm happy to jump on a 20-minute call to walk through any remaining concerns.

Next steps: please confirm by EOD Monday if you want us to send the DocuSign envelope.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance (Commercial)
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0199

Attachment: Commit_Term_Sheet_v2_FINAL_NimbleHealth.pdf (finalized term sheet)
